title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM-Generated NetOps Artifacts: a Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We measure whether adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator increases detection of misconfigurations in LLM-generated network-configuration artifacts. Under a preregistered paired-binary design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) we produced Npairs=720 intent→configuration tasks with a single shared generation per pair (model: gpt-5-mini) and compared (A) baseline: deterministic validator-only versus (B) guarded: validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation. Results (complete paired set): baseline detected 719/720 (0.9986111111), guarded detected 720/720 (1.0000000000); paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI (10000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Interpretation: for this synthetic task bank and validator, sandboxed emulation produced a negligible aggregated detection gain (one additional detection). We report preregistered design choices, exact archived sampling settings, and limitations that constrain external generalization.

sections.introduction: Generative models that translate operator intent into executable network configuration are being proposed as NetOps/AIOps components. Operational safety in such agentic workflows depends heavily on surrounding tooling—validators, verifiers, sandboxed execution, and guarded orchestration—rather than the model alone [1]–[3]. Quantitative evidence on how much sandboxed emulation adds beyond a strong deterministic validator is limited. We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to answer: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) deterministic validator-only and (B) deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired-binary experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) executed end-to-end; (2) an artifact-grounded quantitative result on Npairs=720; (3) a focused discussion of failure modes and external-validity constraints.
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototypes emphasize that generate→validate→repair workflows, plus sandboxed execution, are promising mitigations for LLM-generated artifacts in NetOps and adjacent domains (program/spec verification) [1], [2]. Empirical studies show LLMs can produce configuration errors or hallucinations, and external verifiers or emulators can assist correctness and diagnosis, but cross-vendor, large-scale empirical coverage remains underexplored [3]–[5]. Our work operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of the workflow-centred evaluation called for in that literature and reports a preregistered paired outcome.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) was frozen prior to execution and specified a paired-binary design with shared_initial_candidate semantics (single model generation shared between paired conditions), Npairs=720 confirmatory tasks, planned episodes = 1440, and a pre-specified primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Tasks and scope. The confirmatory task bank used synthetic intent→configuration items (intent_configuration_repair_v1 family) covering abstracted vendor-CLI families and small topology templates; inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance. Model and sampling settings (archived and reported exactly as recorded). Declared model version: gpt-5-mini; provider: openai_responses; requested_model: "gpt-5-mini"; max_output_tokens = 2000; temperature = null (unset) — no claim of deterministic sampling was made; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Execution accounting: maximum_model_calls planned = 1440; model_calls_used = 721 (shared generations 720 plus one repair-stage call). Validator and guarded pipeline. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Guarded pipeline = deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation (emulation detects runtime misbehaviour not captured by static rules). Repair policy and missingness. The preregistered missingness and repair policies allowed up to two deterministic reseeds for parser failures; irrecoverable technical failures were handled per the preregistered plan. In the confirmatory run there were no irrecoverable technical exclusions and a single repair-stage call was recorded and executed according to the preregistered repair policy; its trace is archived. Analysis. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We report exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). All prompts, responses, validator traces, emulation outputs, and analysis artifacts were archived according to the preregistration.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720): contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both); n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only); n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only); n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap (10000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Missingness and deviations: complete_pair_count = 720; no exclusions or preregistration deviations were recorded for the confirmatory analysis. The analysis contingency table is archived as analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced one additional detection out of 720 pairs (0.14 percentage points). This trivial aggregate effect is robust in the archived analysis but must be read in context. Explanatory factors: (a) ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 covered the misconfiguration classes and syntactic patterns in the synthetic task bank, leaving little room for emulation to add detections; (b) synthetic tasks were parser-valid and semantically explicit, increasing validator effectiveness; (c) shared_initial_candidate semantics ensured identical initial model outputs for both conditions, so cross-condition discordance could only arise from emulation observations or the single repair-stage call. Operational implication: when a high-coverage deterministic validator is available and task templates match the studied designs, the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation may be negligible. This does not imply sandboxing is unnecessary: heterogeneity, adversarial inputs, weaker validators, or production-scale complexity can create substantial guarded-pipeline value. Recommendations: future work should evaluate broader/adversarial task banks, multiple model and validator families, and cross-vendor production-scale topologies to locate regimes where guarded pipelines materially improve safety.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an autonomous paired confirmatory experiment comparing deterministic validator-only and validator+sandboxed-emulation pipelines on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated over 720 paired tasks, the guarded pipeline yielded a negligible absolute detection gain (0.0013889) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. The result suggests a potential ceiling effect when validators already achieve near-universal coverage on syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations in curated tasks; broader and adversarial evaluations are required to identify operational regimes where sandboxed execution provides larger marginal benefits.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator reduce ecological diversity and may produce ceiling effects for strong validators.
Single model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.
Shared_initial_candidate design (one initial generation shared across paired conditions) constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.
Sandboxed-emulation fidelity vs production networks is limited to the emulation harness used; vendor/OS nuances and scale effects may alter outcomes.
The observed null-to-very-small aggregate effect on this curated task bank should not be generalized to assert that sandboxed emulation never adds operational value in other NetOps settings.
